topic.title: HBM memory supply as the binding constraint on AI accelerators

questions.primary: Is high-bandwidth memory (HBM) becoming a structural bottleneck for AI accelerator production?
sub: Is demand for HBM growing faster than overall DRAM demand?
How quickly can HBM supply expand, and what limits it?
Can accelerator designs substitute away from HBM?
Who holds pricing power in the HBM supply chain?
What evidence would refute the bottleneck thesis?

thesis: HBM production capacity, constrained by TSV packaging yield and long equipment lead times, is the binding constraint on AI accelerator shipment growth over the next 12-24 months.

facts.statement: A leading HBM supplier stated its HBM capacity is fully committed through next year.
HBM bit demand is growing significantly faster than overall DRAM bit demand according to supplier guidance.

inferences.statement: If capacity is sold out while orders keep rising, HBM suppliers hold near-term pricing power over accelerator vendors.

unknowns: Actual TSV packaging yield rates per supplier (not publicly disclosed).
Timing of next-generation stacked-memory alternatives reaching volume.

bottlenecks.rationale: Demand extreme, supply constrained by packaging equipment lead times, no near-term substitute at required bandwidth.
Strong demand but supply and substitution are more elastic.

competitors.name: Next-gen stacked memory alternatives
competitors.note: Not at volume in the research window.

competitors.name: Status quo (GDDR-based designs)
competitors.note: Insufficient bandwidth for frontier training workloads.

catalysts: Next supplier earnings call with updated HBM capacity guidance
Announcements of new packaging capacity expansion

bear_case.argument: All three major suppliers are adding capacity simultaneously; if AI capex slows even briefly, the bottleneck flips into oversupply as it has in every previous memory cycle.
Architectural changes that reduce memory-bandwidth needs per FLOP would weaken HBM demand growth.

validation_events.supports_if: capacity still sold out and ASPs firm
launch volumes constrained by memory supply
